circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km facility located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, which has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The track represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street-based motorsport venue encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, holding an FIA Grade 1 licence. It hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various support categories including the Supercars Championship event.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. After undergoing modifications and a name change to the A1-Ring, the track returned to hosting the Austrian Grand Prix during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital positioned adjacent to Baku Boulevard, spanning 6. 003 km and ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. It first hosted an F1 race in 2016 as the European Grand Prix before establishing itself as the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Inaugurated in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the first Formula One grand prix ever contested in the Middle East that same year. The FIA Grade 1 facility accommodates various racing series including GP2 and drag racing, along with 24-hour endurance competitions, and features multiple circuit configurations for different events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometres and features a balanced combination of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This 7-kilometre Belgian circuit near Stavelot has been hosting Formula One racing since 1950, when it featured in the championship's inaugural season. The venue regularly stages the Belgian Grand Prix, maintaining an annual presence on the F1 calendar from 1985 onwards, with only two interruptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre racing venue that serves as the permanent home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has hosted multiple racing series including sportscar championships and various touring car competitions throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport venue is primarily recognized for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran from 2004 through 2019 before resuming in 2024. The circuit has expanded its racing calendar to include electric racing events starting in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing facility positioned near the Northamptonshire hamlets of Silverstone and Whittlebury. It inaugurated the British Grand Prix in 1948 and hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950, though the event alternated between three circuits until becoming a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards. The venue additionally serves as the venue for Britain's MotoGP round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km circuit near Budapest, hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986. Built remarkably quickly in just eight months near a major highway outside the city, the track was constructed after plans for a Monaco-style street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected by authorities.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian circuit constructed in 1922 near Milan, earning its reputation as "the Temple of Speed" through notably long straights and rapid corners. Since 1949, the venue has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix, making it the country's premier motor racing event and mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built track.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture operated by Honda Mobilityland. The track, with a 155,000-person capacity, serves as a premier destination for Formula One and Super Formula racing championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, using roads adjacent to the famous Las Vegas Boulevard. The layout passes by several iconic venues and structures including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas hotels and casinos.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both accomplished drivers who tragically died in racing accidents in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue has returned to hosting the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current configuration, though it previously held the race on an earlier layout through 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and an average qualifying speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit architects Apex Circuit Design, the track was built to host the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches 3. 337 km through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, weaving around Monaco's harbour. Though officially named after the principality, it is widely known by its Monte Carlo designation since much of the track occupies that particular district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that was reestablished on the Formula One calendar in 2021 to host the Dutch Grand Prix. The venue's partnership with Formula One is set to conclude after the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a 5. 419 km racing venue situated north of Doha in Qatar, featuring a 1. 068 km main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: São Paulo's Interlagos circuit, officially named after Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace, stretches 4. 309 kilometers and operates in a counterclockwise direction. Established in 1940, the track was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Pace, who tragically died in an aircraft accident eight years earlier.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue located along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah. Since its inaugural year in 2021, the circuit has served as the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, and it began hosting Formula E racing in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street course in Singapore that winds through the Marina Bay area, spanning across the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometer Spanish circuit features a balanced mix of lengthy straightaways and diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test for all racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 accreditation and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its viewing areas.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA track that hosts the United States Formula One Grand Prix alongside NASCAR and various motorcycle racing events. The facility has established itself as a premier motorsport venue in North America, having previously accommodated multiple racing series including IndyCar, sports car championships, and rallycross competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British racing driver competing for Williams in Formula One under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world titles during his 23-season career with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, securing the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and winning Le Mans twice with Toyota, making him the sole driver to have conquered both the Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian racing driver, competes in Formula One for Mercedes and has claimed six Grand Prix victories following his entry into the series in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Haas in the world championship.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabriel Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One, representing the Audi team in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish driver currently racing for Cadillac in Formula One, previously achieved two runner-up championship finishes with Mercedes in consecutive years (2019 and 2020). Across his 13-season career, he has secured 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor who currently races for Alpine in Formula One.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas while primarily competing in European endurance racing. He has participated in seven Formula One races across the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved a notable career victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: French-Algerian driver Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One competition, currently racing for the Red Bull Racing team.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver competing for Ferrari, holding a shared record of seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads in multiple statistical categories including race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg is a German Formula One driver currently racing for Audi. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver Charles Leclerc races for Ferrari in Formula One, having achieved nine career Grand Prix victories over nine seasons. He came closest to the world championship in 2022 when he finished as runner-up in the drivers' standings.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW's WRT team and part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series for Trackhouse Racing. He previously had two separate stints in Formula One, racing from 2014-2020 before returning for the 2022-2024 seasons.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris represents Great Britain in Formula One racing and currently drives for McLaren. The British driver secured the 2025 World Drivers' Championship title with the team and has accumulated 12 race victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, currently competes in Formula One with Haas. He previously achieved a Grand Prix victory in 2021 while driving for Alpine, winning the Hungarian round of the championship.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. The former Red Bull driver finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship and has claimed six race victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo, known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: The British driver competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has claimed seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. He previously raced in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons, and has also competed in IMSA SportsCar Championship prototype racing.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese racing driver, held a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls during his Formula One tenure from 2021 to 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen races for Red Bull Racing and has claimed four consecutive world titles between 2021 and 2024. Over his 12-season Formula One career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, a Chinese racing driver, currently holds a reserve position with Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the sport's top tier between 2022 and 2024, maintaining a unique distinction as the sole Chinese driver to have raced in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from its Enstone base since 2021 under the Alpine brand, this French-licensed team represents Renault's factory effort in Formula One until the manufacturer's withdrawal at the end of 2025. The squad's most notable achievement came through Esteban Ocon's victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, and currently competes with Mercedes power units having previously used them during its Lotus era in 2015.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through multiple team entities, currently operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco branding in the sport.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian luxury manufacturer Ferrari, represents the sport's longest-running and most accomplished outfit, participating continuously since the championship's inaugural 1950 season. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their distinctive emblem, the team remains a foundational institution in Formula One history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the squad entering the championship in 2016. Leadership recently transitioned when Ayao Komatsu assumed the team principal role in early 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had helmed the operation since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering firm established itself through endurance racing success, including victory at Le Mans in 1989, before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. The team competed for over three decades, becoming the fourth-longest-serving constructor by race entries before ceasing operations in 2025, when Audi acquired its operations to establish the foundation for their own Formula One programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under the ownership of Mumtalakat Holding Company. The team competes in the sport under commercial sponsorship partnerships.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 in both engine supply and team ownership roles. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas outfit, based in Brackley with a German licence, underwent a restructuring in 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal partner alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff. The team carries the iconic "Silver Arrows" designation, a longstanding nickname for Mercedes entries.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that debuted in 2024 as part of Red Bull's multi-team structure alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an operational presence near Milton Keynes, the team operates as the second racing division under Austrian ownership while maintaining its identity as an independent Italian constructor.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team functions as Red Bull's second constructor entry in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and owned by Red Bull GmbH since its 2005 establishment. The team was led by Christian Horner throughout its first two decades before Laurent Mekies took over as team principal in 2025. Red Bull GmbH also operates a second Formula One outfit through Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One team founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding an earlier unsuccessful racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026 and operates as both a racing team and constructor.
